# stdx

> Extensions to std: compound assignment, for-in loops, match and assertions.

[source](../../registry/stdx.pkg) · truck

Shorthands that `std` doesn't have. Every package here `expand`s into
`std` constructs, so they work with every backend and have no backend
packages of their own.

```
use std
use stdx

let total = 0
for n in make([int], 3)
  total += n + 1
end
assert total == 3
```

| package | syntax | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `stdx/add_assign` | `x += y` | `x = x + y` |
| `stdx/sub_assign` | `x -= y` | `x = x - y` |
| `stdx/mul_assign` | `x *= y` | `x = x * y` |
| `stdx/div_assign` | `x /= y` | `x = x / y` |
| `stdx/mod_assign` | `x %= y` | `x = x % y` |
| `stdx/forin` | `for x in xs ... end` | a loop over a slice's elements or a string's bytes |
| `stdx/match` | `match x`, `case a, b`, `else`, `end` | an `if`/`elif` chain comparing `x` with `==` |
| `stdx/assert` | `assert cond` | stop with status 2 and the position if `cond` is false |

`stdx` is a separate truck, not part of `std`, so its words (`in`,
`match`, `case`, `assert`) are only reserved in programs that use it,
and programs and lock files that only use `std` are unaffected. Use single packages
(`use stdx/forin`) to take just one.
